question: Atul invests a sum of ₹5400 and Nirmal invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Nirmal gets ₹480 more interest than Atul, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest difference = (Difference in Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

480 = [(10200 − 5400) × R × 5] ÷ 100

480 = (4800 × R × 5) ÷ 100

480 = 240 × R

R = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Nirmal's principal (P₁) = ₹10200

Atul's principal (P₂) = ₹5400

Time (T) = 5 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹480
